correctness.rationale: An affine contraction gives the unique stationary qubit; its exact coherence leads by SLD to a full-rank rational QFI for every nonresonant phase. The exact derivative is \(xP_t(x)/A^4\), and a uniform one-sign-change argument plus endpoint signs proves one simple positive maximizing root. Scaling the polynomial at phase detuning gives the unique root limit and sharp Fisher constant. SymPy identities, an independent spectral-SLD calculation at 24 points, fixed-point checks and root brackets corroborate the analytic proof. The exact resonance is excluded.

originality.rationale: The stationary geometric-age mixture and standard single-qubit QFI formula are known; the exact one-positive-root optimizer and universal punctured-detuning scaling were not found in the inspected published primary source or matched research records. The relevant prior results concern quantum coherences, two-qubit correlations, generic continuous-time reset response, or sequential readout; none yields the stated phase-dependent algebraic classification without additional argument. Unlocated general coverage remains a risk.
residual_risks: Search indexes and accessible literature may miss a more general exact QFI optimization theorem; publication priority is not independently certified.
The broader O'Connor article was not exhaustively read; its accessible Fisher-rate setup uses a different observable and does not present decisive coverage.
The present result is a stationary unconditioned snapshot theorem. Statements involving preparation cost, reset history, or exact pure-state resonance require separate analysis.

value.rationale: The reset frequency of a stroboscopic sensor controls a nontrivial competition between phase accumulation and stationary mixing. The theorem completely and rigorously resolves stationary unconditioned phase-precision optimization over the full nonresonant phase domain, supplies a simple opposite-phase calibration and a sharp singular near-resonance design scaling. It is more than a parameter substitution or a sample optimum, though it is not a cost-normalized device protocol.
